name: Leeuwin Current
scope: Source-convention Leeuwin component from the North West Cape regional gate near 22 degrees S, southward around Cape Leeuwin and eastward into the central Great Australian Bight. Nominal eastern gate 130 degrees E uses the source's winter water-mass penetration convention; alternative 125 degrees E tests a shorter central-Bight naming convention. Excludes the North West Shelf, offshore eddies, South Australian and Zeehan components. Not the full 5,500 km boundary-flow system.
layer: Shelf-edge upper-ocean reference geography; no fixed-depth or diagnosed velocity axis.
time_convention: Editorial reference route under the source's autumn/winter southern-extension convention; not a simultaneous or climatological measured axis, nor a guaranteed summer path.
source_locator: Ridgway and Condie (2004), section 2 paragraph 10 (North West Cape domain gate); section 7 paragraph 50 (winter signature near 130 degrees E); section 9 paragraph 56 (Leeuwin component through central Great Australian Bight). Paragraphs 57–58 name downstream components separately.
source_citation: Ridgway and Condie (2004), The 5500-km-long boundary flow off western and southern Australia, Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans 109, C04017, doi:10.1029/2003JC001921.
source_license: Factual geography only; no source prose, figure, source curve or velocity field packaged.
coordinate_selection: OSW selects coarse offshore waypoints. The source supplies naming regions and broad gates, not these intermediate coordinates or a published shelf contour. Initial 121–127 degrees E chords crossed the coarse land mask and were moved offshore before retention. This clearance does not verify shelf-edge alignment. The 125 degrees E alternative is an OSW interpretation of central-Bight extent, not a source-reported termination coordinate.

alternative_routes.interpretation: OSW shorter central-Bight naming interpretation; not a measured source termination.

scenario_rule: Two eastern naming conventions crossed with longitude shifts (-0.15/0/+0.15 degrees) and independent endpoint latitude shifts (-0.25/0/+0.25 degrees): 54 editorial scenarios. No empirical current-axis error distribution implied.
remaining_gates: Scientific review of Leeuwin naming/penetration conventions and the eastern gate.
Check offshore route against reproducible bathymetric or layer-specific velocity geometry.
